name: 1619 Prairie Avenue — stone-front house with its swell bay, for now wearing the front of Hamline's house next door at 1621 (T-2439), K01 frontage assembly

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its north (low-v) side: the draft's origin moved 5.9 m toward the street and 2.87 m north along its own frame, onto the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s20fp-1619-b1), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.607 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south.
placement.symbolic_location: 1619 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1619 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1619-b1) in the lot frame: the stone front's face at 19.2 m from the rear lot line's middle, the north wall at v -2.87 and the south wall on the lot line at 5.59, and the rear wall where the trace's north part ends (5.9 m), so 13.3 m deep and 8.46 m along the front. The 0.6 m jog the trace draws in the north wall's rear half is not built. The bow stands on it (form.bays); the range behind its south part is a rear wing (form.rear_wings).

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement, and a third in the steep roof, lit by the wall gable over the bow: the Building Budget drawing's own count (the raised basement with its grilled lights; the principal and second storeys, which the bow carries to its balcony at the wall head; above that only the gable's three short lights, about 0.9 m high against the second storey's 2.2 m, between pinnacles). The 1911 sheet prints '4' over the house. The two are not reconciled: the sheet may count the raised basement and the roof storey, or the house may have been raised after 1886, which no picture shows. Built to the drawing, the house's only picture; a photograph after 1886 decides it (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1619-hamline-2420/README.md).

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a brick house; the drawing draws the front in coursed smooth ashlar and the south side wall plain.

principal_floor_m.note: 1.4 m over grade, the draft's and 1634's, inside the K01 contract's range. The drawing's raised basement reads about 1.5-1.7 m through its camera (building_budget_front.json), within that solve's own spread.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 3.9 m and 3.9 m, the two storeys the bow carries. Through the drawing's camera the second floor reads at about 5.3 m and the bow's balcony at about 8.9 m; the wall head is put at 9.2 m so the bow can rise to 8.2 m under the K10 cornice's bed moulding. No dimension is printed on the drawing.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's and 1634's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: The drawing draws the front in smooth coursed ashlar, light, with plain joints, and the basement's courses heavier; it is monochrome, so the stone is chosen: K02's Bedford limestone, the light dressed stone of Chicago's mid-1880s fronts, smooth over two rusticated base courses. The 1911 sheet says only 'stone'. Replaceable by any description naming the stone.

street_front_trim.note: The north strip's door and the lights over it: a K09 cornice-hood lintel over the door's storey and K01's flat stone lintel over the second storey's light. The drawing's round-arched entrance and the carved panel over it are T-2422's to build.

wall_head.note: The drawing's moulded stone cornice (T-2460), K10's `k10.cornice.moulded_stone`: one section read off the plate, about 0.35 m deep where it runs round the bow's top and carries the balcony (8.2-8.55 m on the bow's face through its camera), swept along the street front under the K05 soffit (8.24-8.6 m), corner to corner between the side walls' parapets under the gable roof (T-2459) and capped at both corners, and stopped at the bow's junctions, where the bow carries the same section round its own plan (bays.eaves). It replaces K10's bracketed timber cornice (scrolled brackets and a bed moulding), which the drawing does not draw. The eave's timber over it (the K05 soffit and fascia) is painted to read as the stone, as a cornice of the period was (`paint`); the drawing shows one stone cornice and no eave above it, and the colour is reconstructed (L-k01-1619-stone-cornice-2460). The dormer face is K10's pedimented face, the drawing's wall gable (T-2428): its horizontal and raking cornices are the kit's, the nearest it comes to the drawing's moulded stone gable.

roof_form.note: A gable roof whose ridge runs along the front (T-2459), reconstructed as a whole because half of it is unseen: the drawing slates a steep slope facing the street behind the wall gable and carries the house's SOUTH side wall up above it as a crow-stepped parapet rising from the front corner to a tall stack, so the slope meets that wall and rises with it, which K01's hip (whose south face falls away from the wall) cannot do. What lies behind the ridge the drawing does not show: the rear slope falls to the rear wall's head (gable_roof).

roof_pitch_deg.note: 45 degrees, the K01 contract's steepest ordinary pitch, for the street slope: the drawing's slates rise behind the gable about as steeply as the gable itself (about 50 degrees), and the third storey is in the roof. Through the drawing's camera the parapet's head, at the stack, stands about 13.5 m up and about 4 m behind the front, which a 45-degree slope from the 9.2 m wall head reaches 4.23 m back (gable_roof.ridge_back_m).

stair_tread_m.note: A tread that brings the stoop inside the 3.8 m front yard the sheet leaves.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A short landing: the front yard is 3.8 m deep.

stoop_width_m.note: Inside the north strip, clear of the bow.

entrance_bay.note: The door in the front's north strip, as the drawing draws it beside the bow (its round-arched recess is T-2422's). 'south' is K01's name for the low-v end of the front; on the east side of the avenue the plan's v runs south, so that end is the north end on the ground.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 8.46 m front, low v to high v: the door bay in the middle of the north strip (s 0-3.79, the sheet's front north of the bow) with a light over it in each upper storey, and the bow's centre. The drawing's north strip is narrower against its bow than the sheet's; the sheet controls the plan.

bays.note: The swell bay. Its PLACE and SIZE are the 1911 sheet's (s20fp-1619-b1's stone part bulges 1.02 m from the front over v 3.79-7.55, a 3.76 m chord); its HEIGHT and LIGHTS are the drawing's: it rises from grade through the principal and second storeys to the cornice, as the drawing carries it (5.3 m and 2.94 m: its wall top at 8.24 m, the foot of the street front's moulded stone cornice, T-2460), and its eaves ARE that cornice: the same K10 section swept round its plan (`eaves.cornice`), so the two read as one moulding; until T-2460 it stopped at 8.2 m under a plain timber eave, clear of a bracketed cornice's bed moulding, two lights a storey either side of a central pier (at -25 and +25 degrees on the bow's arc), and it is laid in the front's stone. Its top is a nearly flat painted-tin deck, where the drawing's balcony stands (the rail is T-2422's). The lights' sizes are the drawing's through its camera, rounded.

side_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the house's NORTH side wall (K01's 'south' wall, the low-v side; s from the rear), toward the 1.3 m gap the sheet leaves to 1613-1615. No picture shows this wall.

north_bays.note: None: the house's SOUTH side wall (K01's 'north', high v) is built blank, as the drawing draws it — a plain shaded wall from the ground to its stepped parapet, standing on the lot line toward 1621.

rear_bays.note: One window a storey in the rear wall's north part (s from the high-v end), the part the rear range does not cover.

rear_wings.note: The rear range the 1911 sheet draws behind the main body's south part (s20fp-1619-b1 p2: the main brick part runs on 6.0 m past the rear wall over its south 5.69 m, flush with the south wall). Its PLACE and storeys are the sheet's (the same part, so the same count as the house); its windows, heights and flat tin deck are reconstructed. The sheet's half-round frame porch behind it is not built: K01 has no porch.

sash_by_storey.note: The north strip's and the side and rear walls' sash, storey by storey; the second storey's light over the door is narrow, as the drawing's.

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the principal windows, as 1634's; the drawing's two under the bow are its own.

roof_covering.note: Slate: the drawing hatches the roof behind the gable as slating. Pennsylvania slate, copper flashing and ridge roll, the K04 kit's commonest slate roof.

dormer.note: The roof storey's WALL GABLE (T-2428), read off the drawing through its solved camera: the street wall carried up over the bow as a steep pedimented gable (the K05 dormer with its face on the wall's plane, no setback), 3.3 m across and 0.47 m north of the bow's centre line as the drawing sets it (v 5.2), its face 2.0 m to the eave and pitched 50 degrees, so the pediment's foot lands at about 10.9 m and its apex at about 13.05 m against the drawing's 10.9-11.0 m and 13.1 m; three short segment-headed lights (K06's one-over-one segmental sash, 0.75 by 0.95 m, 1.1 m apart, sills 0.3 m over the wall head) each under a block of seven radiating voussoirs 0.2 m over its crown; a recessed panel in the pediment; a turned finial at the apex; and a square pinnacle shaft either side of the face, 1.95 m off its centre, rising from under the wall head to a cap and pyramid at about 11.65-12.2 m (the drawing's two caps read at about 11.5 m and 11.9 m: it draws them unequal, and they are built level). What the drawing shows is the gable, its three lights and their heads, the voussoirs, the cornices, the panel, the finial and the two pinnacles; every size is read through a camera good to about 10 %, the pinnacles' square plan, the pyramid tops (the drawing's are carved), the panel's depth, the lights' sash and the stone are reconstructed (L-k01-1619-hamline-wall-gable-2428). The roof behind, the crow-stepped south parapet and the stone cornice at the bow's top are T-2429's.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks carried up in the south side wall's parapet (T-2459), 1.0 m along the wall and 0.9 m deep (so the first stack's sides stand clear of the parapet head's risers), their outer faces in the wall's plane: the first at the ridge, where the drawing's tall stack stands at the head of the crow steps, its top at 15.03 m (1.6 m over the ridge) as the drawing's reads through its camera (about y 80 px against the render's 80, its left edge at about x 478 against 477); the second, over the rear rooms, reconstructed at the same height. The drawing's panelled shafts and corbelled cap are built plain.

rainwater.note: No gutter or downpipe is built (T-2459): the drawing draws none on the front, and K01's half-round gutter runs only round a hip's eaves, where this roof's side walls are parapets. How the roof drained is not read; T-2420's copper gutters and pipes, themselves reconstructed (no picture shows them), are withdrawn with the hip.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, as the drawing's lights are drawn with one meeting rail and drawn-back curtains.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a straight stoop; the front yard is 3.8 m, the sheet's front at 19.2 m against the street line at 23.0 m. The drawing's stoop climbs beside the strip; T-2422 builds it as drawn.

gable_roof.note: Read off the drawing where it shows the roof, reconstructed where it does not. The roof's ridge 4.23 m behind the front wall, at 13.43 m, where the drawing's parapet reaches its stack (about 13.5 m up and about 4 m back through its camera, building_budget_front.json); the rear slope falls from it to the rear wall's head, at about 25 degrees, which no picture shows. The house's SOUTH side wall (K01's 'north', high v) is carried up as the drawing's crow-stepped parapet: five steps up the street slope, as the drawing draws them (its kneeler blocks at about y 225, 205, 185, 165 and 145 px in the panel), each coped and clearing the slates by K05's 0.3 m upstand, to a level head 0.3 m (the upstand) over the ridge, at 13.73 m, where the stack stands; the same five steps down the rear slope are reconstructed. The NORTH side wall (K01's 'south'), which no picture shows, is carried up as a plain coped parapet on the slopes, reconstructed (L-k01-1619-gable-roof-2459).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '4-storey brick dwelling (D), stone (blue) front with a curved bay'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: 'Houses, Prairie Ave. — Treat and Foltz, Archts. — J. H. Hamline Esq. / G. Farwell Esq.' The Building Budget (Chicago), June 188- (the year is cut off on the reproduced page). Pen perspective of two stone-fronted town houses, with a small plan inset. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, the 1811 S. Prairie page (captioned there '1811 S. Prairie Ave.', a mislabel).
what_it_supplies: the swell bay's height (grade to the third floor) and its two lights a storey
three storeys over a raised basement, the third in a wall gable over the bow
the entrance's place in the north strip, round-arched and recessed
the slated roof, the stepped south parapet and its stack
what_it_does_not_supply: the plan: the 1911 Sanborn sheet's trace controls it, and the drawing's north strip is narrower than the sheet's
the north side wall, the rear and anything the 1886 design lost or gained by 1904

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2420 (piece 1 of T-2419, of T-1868) refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id from the house's one picture, Treat & Foltz's drawing in The Building Budget (June 188-, probably 1886; building_budget_1886_06_hamline_farwell_houses), read against the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20, which controls the plan. The main body is rebuilt on the K01 frontage assembly: a K02 smooth limestone street front on K03 brick sides and rear, the drawing's full-height swell bay on K08's bow at the sheet's own chord and rise, rising from grade to the third floor, the door in the north strip on a K07 stoop, a K10 bracketed cornice and a slated K04/K05 hip, and (T-2428) the drawing's wall gable over the bow: three segment-headed lights under radiating voussoirs, the pediment with its recessed panel and finial, and two pinnacles, and the sheet's rear range on K01's rear wings. (T-2459) the roof behind the gable as the drawing slates it: a street slope as steep as the gable to a ridge along the front, and the house's south side wall carried up above it as a crow-stepped parapet to the tall stack at the ridge (k01_gable_roof). What the drawing shows and is not yet built — the stone cornice at the bow's top (T-2460); the round-arched entrance, the side stoop, the balcony rail and the grilled basement arches (T-2422) — is listed open in its match record (data/reference_views/house_1619_prairie/building_budget_front.match.json). Everything not read is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1619-hamline-swell-front-2420 and, for the wall gable, L-k01-1619-hamline-wall-gable-2428 and, for the roof, L-k01-1619-gable-roof-2459.
